n: David doesn’t ask to escape correction, but asks God not to correct him in anger. He knows he needs discipline, yet longs for it to come with mercy.

f.w: rebuke me not in thy wrath

n: He feels God’s correction like arrows lodged in his body and a hand pressing hard on him.

f.w: thine arrows stick fast in me

n: His body has no health and his bones no rest because of his sin. David sees a close link between spiritual guilt and physical suffering.
His sins have risen over his head like floodwater, and they press on him like a load too heavy to carry.

f.w: as an heavy burden they are too heavy for me

n: He describes festering wounds — a raw picture of how sin, left untreated, rots and spreads. He owns that it came from his foolishness.

f.g: In Hebrew wisdom writing, folly means moral rebellion, not just a lack of intelligence.

n: He is bent over with grief, walking around in mourning all day.

f.g: Literally “I go about in black,” as one dressed for mourning.

n: His body burns with sickness; nothing in him feels healthy.

f.g: The lower back and sides; the seat of strength.

n: Weak and crushed, he groans aloud from the turmoil inside.

f.g: Groaned or cried out in anguish.

n: A tender turn: Lord, you already know everything I long for; even my sighs aren’t hidden from you.

f.w: my groaning is not hid from thee

n: His heart races, his strength is gone, and even the light in his eyes has faded.
Loved ones and friends keep their distance from his suffering; even relatives stay far off. Suffering can be lonely.
Meanwhile, enemies set traps for him and plot against him with lies all day long.
David responds by not responding: like a deaf and mute man, he doesn’t answer their attacks.

f.g: Unable to speak, mute — not a comment on intelligence.

f.w: as a dumb man that openeth not his mouth

n: He has no rebuttal in his mouth. He leaves his defense to God.
Here is why he stays silent: his hope is in the Lord, who will answer for him.
He asks God to hear him so his enemies don’t gloat — they puff themselves up the moment he slips.
David feels ready to collapse, and his pain never leaves his sight.

f.g: About to stumble or fall; “halt” means limp or be lame.

n: He confesses openly and feels true sorrow for his sin — the heart of repentance.

f.w: I will be sorry for my sin

n: Meanwhile, his enemies are healthy and strong and grow in number, though they hate him without reason.
They repay his good with evil, opposing him precisely because he follows what is good.
Two final cries: don’t abandon me; don’t stay far away.
The psalm ends with an urgent plea: hurry to help me, Lord, my salvation. The answer isn’t yet given, but hope is still voiced.
